findings.explanation: HOL4 defines HD by the single clause HD (h::t) = h. Define makes this a primitive recursion, so Prim_rec.new_recursive_definition introduces HD by new_specification (Prim_rec.sml:259-285). I found no saved theorem that fixes HD []. Lean adds the clause HD [] = ARB, so it proves HD [] = ARB, EL 0 [] = ARB and, with LAST, HD [] = LAST []. HOL4 leaves these equations open. SEG in this module and OUTL in Basic avoid this by using Classical.epsilon over the specification.
findings.repair:
noncomputable def HD {α : Type u} [Nonempty α] : List α → α :=
  Classical.epsilon (fun HD : List α → α => ∀ h t, HD (h :: t) = h)
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.Prelude.List

example {α : Type} [Nonempty α] : HD ([] : List α) = ARB := by rw [HD]

example {α : Type} [Nonempty α] : HD ([] : List α) = LAST ([] : List α) := by rw [HD, LAST]
findings.hol4_check: ?hd:num list -> num. (!h t. hd (h::t) = h) /\ hd [] <> ARB

findings.explanation: HOL4's LAST_DEF has only the clause LAST (h::t) = if t = [] then h else LAST t. It is a primitive recursion introduced by new_specification, so LAST [] is unspecified. The saved theorems about LAST that I found either concern non-empty lists or leave LAST [] undetermined. Lean adds the clause LAST [] = ARB, so it proves LAST [] = ARB and LAST [] = HD []. HOL4 leaves both open. FRONT is different: HOL4 does save FRONT [] = [], so its Lean clause is correct.
findings.repair:
noncomputable def LAST {α : Type u} [Nonempty α] : List α → α :=
  Classical.epsilon (fun LAST : List α → α =>
    ∀ h t, LAST (h :: t) = if t = [] then h else LAST t)
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.Prelude.List

example {α : Type} [Nonempty α] : LAST ([] : List α) = ARB := by rw [LAST]
findings.hol4_check: ?lst:num list -> num. (!h t. lst (h::t) = if t = [] then h else lst t) /\ lst [] <> ARB
